five_minutes: BOJ minutes suggest the central bank remains dovish, keeping Japanese yields low and limiting upside for the USD, which eases pressure on the INR.
RBI Bulletin flags a widening credit‑deposit gap, warning of margin pressure on banks and hinting at possible RBI liquidity action.
The RBI’s 24 bn rupee Treasury Bill auction will likely anchor short‑term yields near 5.3‑5.5%, supporting the current G‑sec curve.
FEMA amendment tightens export‑import documentation, potentially raising working‑capital costs for IT services exporters.
The Adani Group settlement order removes a regulatory overhang, likely stabilising sentiment in Indian equities and related corporate debt.

Gold and silver will NOT rise further even in a recession, because they are already at all-time highs
Nifty 29-Sep futures will fall below 23,000 before expiry

buckets.label: What you need to know today

items.headline: BOJ minutes signal continued dovish stance, keeping yields low and limiting USD upside
items.what_happened: The Bank of Japan released minutes from its July 30‑31 policy meeting.
items.why_it_matters: A dovish stance keeps Japanese yields subdued, reducing demand for higher‑yielding USD assets and easing potential INR depreciation pressure.

items.headline: Japan’s Services PPI shows modest rise, keeping inflation pressures limited
items.what_happened: The Bank of Japan released the Services Producer Price Index for August.
items.why_it_matters: A modest increase suggests limited inflationary pressure in Japan, supporting the BOJ’s dovish stance and keeping global yield differentials stable.

items.headline: Strong El Niño forecast could boost global commodity demand and pressure Indian food prices
items.what_happened: The International Research Institute warned that El Niño may become very strong by late 2026.
items.why_it_matters: A strong El Niño can tighten global agricultural supply, lifting commodity prices and feeding into Indian food‑price inflation, which may affect RBI policy and the INR.

items.headline: RBI Bulletin highlights widening credit‑deposit gap, signaling margin pressure on banks
items.what_happened: The RBI’s September 2026 bulletin published articles on the state of the economy, credit‑deposit divergence and private corporate investment.
items.why_it_matters: A widening gap squeezes bank margins and may prompt RBI liquidity measures, affecting bank stocks, G‑sec yields and credit growth.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: RBI amends classification and valuation rules for financial institution investment portfolios
items.what_happened: The RBI issued amendment directions on classification, valuation and operation of investment portfolios for all‑India financial institutions.
items.why_it_matters: Changed valuation norms affect banks’ balance‑sheet accounting, potentially altering reported profitability and influencing credit‑deposit dynamics.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: RBI sets WMA limit at 50,000 crore rupees for Oct‑Mar FY27, signalling potential fresh market loan floatation
items.what_happened: The RBI, in consultation with the Government, fixed the Ways and Means Advances ceiling for the second half of FY26‑27 at 50,000 crore rupees.
items.why_it_matters: A higher WMA limit gives the government flexibility to issue market loans, which can affect Treasury yields and fiscal financing costs.

items.headline: Adani Group settlement order removes regulatory overhang, likely steadies equity sentiment
items.what_happened: SEBI issued a settlement order in the matter of Adani Group companies.
items.why_it_matters: Resolving the regulatory issue removes a source of uncertainty for Adani‑linked equities and debt, supporting market stability.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: RBI OMO sale of G‑sec places yields at ~6.67% on 10‑yr bonds
items.what_happened: The RBI sold government securities on Sep 28 with a cut‑off yield of 6.6676% for the 2029 issue and similar levels for other tenors.
items.why_it_matters: The cut‑off yields set a ceiling for the 10‑yr G‑sec curve, influencing bond pricing, fund flows and the cost of corporate borrowing.

items.headline: RBI auctions 24 bn rupees of Treasury Bills, anchoring short‑term yields near 5.3‑5.5%
items.what_happened: The RBI announced auctions of 91‑day, 182‑day and 364‑day Treasury Bills totaling 24 bn rupees.
items.why_it_matters: The auction size and expected pricing will keep overnight repo and short‑term G‑sec yields in the 5.3‑5.5% band, shaping money‑market liquidity and bond market positioning.

items.headline: State governments auction 22,200 crore rupees of securities, adding supply to the bond market
items.what_happened: State governments offered to sell securities totaling 22,200 crore rupees across multiple tenors.
items.why_it_matters: Increased state‑level sovereign supply can lift yields on comparable tenors, affecting the broader G‑sec curve and corporate bond pricing.

items.headline: RBI VRRR auction clears at 5.24%, setting overnight repo floor
items.what_happened: The overnight variable rate reverse repo auction closed with a cut‑off and weighted average rate of 5.24%.
items.why_it_matters: The VRR rate sets the lower bound for short‑term money‑market rates, influencing G‑sec yields and banks’ funding costs.

items.headline: Settlement order for Nippon Yield Maximiser AIF clarifies compliance, may ease fund‑raising for alternative assets
items.what_happened: SEBI issued a settlement order in the Nippon Yield Maximiser AIF Scheme I matter.
items.why_it_matters: Resolution of the AIF compliance issue restores confidence for investors in alternative funds, supporting inflows into the sector.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: FEMA amendment tightens export‑import documentation, raising compliance costs for exporters
items.what_happened: The RBI issued amendment regulations to the Foreign Exchange Management Act governing export and import of goods and services.
items.why_it_matters: Stricter documentation can increase working‑capital requirements for IT services and other exporters, affecting cash flows and profitability.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.
